turns: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?
results.answer: Minneapolis (MSP) is the most exposed Midwest hub to winter disruption, with a winter score of 48.2. That is moderate, not high. Chicago (39.9) and Detroit (37.4) follow, also moderate. Kansas City is next at 33.8, which is just inside moderate. Indianapolis (30.7) and Columbus (30.1) are low. No Midwest hub reaches the high band (66 or above), so this ranking is relative. MSP's main drivers are 146.4 days/yr with a minimum temperature at or below 0 C and 20.4 days/yr with snowfall of 1 cm or more. Chicago has 103.6 freeze days and 18.6 snow days per year. Chicago and Detroit are a close call, so their order is not meaningful. Indianapolis and Columbus are also a close call.

turns: Compare Miami and Houston in terms of hurricane and flood exposure.
results.answer: Miami has the higher hurricane/wind exposure, and Houston has far higher flood exposure. Wind: Miami scores 51.9 (moderate) and Houston 43.1 (moderate). Flood: Houston scores 74.7 (high) and Miami 32.4 (low). Houston has 23.6 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain, against 9.2 for Miami. It has 4.2 days/yr with at least 50 mm, against 2.2, and 7 FEMA flood declarations, against 2. Neither hub is high on wind, and Houston's composite is 39.0 (moderate) against Miami's 22.7 (low).
